item.text: I’ll work from the prior candidate set in memory and write only omitted proposals to `followup.tsv`, without reopening either file.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec5/luna/followup.tsv <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	karsi_anlati	WLC:Ezek.14.14	Noah delivers only himself	The commentary's Noah scene includes a son who cannot shelter himself by lineage; Ezekiel names Noah among the righteous who could save only their own lives in a judged land, limiting the refuge righteousness provides.
strong	tevrat	karsi_anlati	WLC:Ezek.14.20	sons and daughters not delivered	The commentary notes lineage as a possible refuge but recounts Noah's son perishing; Ezekiel explicitly says even Noah could not deliver sons or daughters, making kinship no guarantee against judgment.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ruth.2.12	refuge under God's wings	The commentary calls asr a shelter for the endangered; Boaz blesses Ruth for coming to take refuge under the wings of Israel's God, using the same protective image for a vulnerable outsider.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ruth.3.9	kinsman-redeemer spreads his wing	The commentary says a person's lineage can be a refuge; Ruth asks Boaz, her redeemer, to spread his wing over her, joining kinship protection to the sheltering image.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.14.13	stand and see God's salvation	The commentary describes a calamity with no apparent exit and rescue from it; trapped Israel is told not to fear but to stand and see the Lord's salvation, making trust communal at the edge of danger.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Exod.14.22	Israel crosses the sea on dry ground	The commentary's Noah scene concerns water and a failed human refuge; Exodus says the people pass through the divided sea on dry ground, depicting deliverance as a path opened through the danger.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.34.20	many afflictions; the Lord delivers	The commentary places a person in loss and peril; the psalm says the righteous have many afflictions but the Lord delivers them from all, joining endurance of trouble to rescue.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.107.28	cry in distress; storm stilled	The commentary pictures people needing shelter and escape; sailors cry to the Lord in their trouble, and he stills the storm, making deliverance an answer to danger at sea.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.107.29	calm after the waves	The commentary's endangered person seeks safety; the psalm says God makes the storm a calm and its waves quiet, specifying the change from peril to safety.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.107.30	delivered to a desired haven	The commentary names asr as a refuge and salvation place; the sailors are glad when the sea grows quiet and God brings them to their desired harbor, supplying a concrete destination for rescue.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.124.8	escaped bird; snare broken	The commentary joins clinging with rescue from a pit; the community says it escaped like a bird from a fowler's snare when the trap broke, an image of release from an inescapable-looking danger.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.14.26	children have refuge in fear of the Lord	The commentary says lineage can be a refuge; Proverbs says the one who fears the Lord has strong confidence and his children have a refuge, locating family safety in trust in God.
strong	tevrat	karsi_anlati	WLC:Ps.27.11	God takes in the abandoned	The commentary mentions lineage as a sheltering root; the psalm says that even if father and mother forsake the speaker, the Lord will take him in, making divine refuge survive family failure.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Deut.33.27	dwelling place and everlasting arms	The commentary develops refuge and armor as shelter; Moses calls the eternal God Israel's dwelling place with everlasting arms beneath, combining a safe home and protective arms.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.17.7	trust in the Lord as security	The commentary identifies iman with entering safety; Jeremiah blesses the person who trusts in the Lord and makes the Lord his trust, stating the security relation directly.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.17.8	no fear in drought; still bears fruit	The commentary joins faith, righteous action, and escape from loss; Jeremiah's tree planted by water has no fear when heat or drought comes and does not cease bearing fruit, linking trust to continued life and deeds.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.35.3	strengthen weak hands	The commentary describes the sabīr as one who stands with the group; Isaiah tells hearers to strengthen weak hands and steady feeble knees, making mutual support a response to fear.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.35.4	say to the fearful, God comes to save	The commentary says people mutually counsel one another in truth and patience; Isaiah instructs them to tell anxious hearts to be strong because God comes to save, supplying the content and purpose of encouragement.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.33.16	refuge in rocky heights; sure provisions	The commentary makes asr a shelter and armor a form of protection; Isaiah says the secure person dwells on heights, with rocky fortresses for refuge and bread and water assured.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 2:2	steadfast in a time of calamity	The commentary associates sabr with calamity and endurance; Sirach tells the person serving God to set the heart right and be steadfast rather than panic in adversity.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 2:4	accept adversity; be patient in reversals	The commentary records a branch sense of sabr as an ordeal with no exit; Sirach says to accept what comes and be patient when humbled, treating adversity as a test of fidelity.
strong	tevrat	motif	Sirach 2:6	trust God; he will help	The commentary calls iman security and sabr patience; Sirach joins trust, hope, and God's help, showing the expected refuge for a person enduring trial.
strong	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Genesis Rabbah 32:6	Noah delays entering the ark	The commentary identifies believers with those who enter safety; a midrash commonly located at Genesis Rabbah 32:6 portrays Noah as hesitating until the waters press him into the ark, complicating that entry with a reading of delayed trust (the locator is from memory).
strong	incil	yorum_gelenegi	1 Clement 12	Rahab's scarlet sign shelters her household	The commentary joins a sheltering place, lineage, and clinging; 1 Clement retells Rahab's rescue by faith and hospitality, with a scarlet cord marking the house where her family is spared, making a household's refuge visible.
strong	incil	yorum_gelenegi	Shepherd of Hermas, Vision 3 (tower vision)	tower as the Church and entry into it	The commentary pictures a secure place reached by those who escape loss; Hermas's tower vision interprets the tower as the Church and distinguishes people by whether they can be built into it, giving the secure-community image an early Christian reading.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Mark.4.38	\"we are perishing\" in the storm	The commentary glosses khusr as perishing; the disciples in a storm wake Jesus with the fear that they are perishing, placing the word in a concrete scene of danger.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Mark.4.39	Jesus stills wind and sea	The commentary asks what shelter can save a person in danger; Jesus rebukes the wind and commands the sea to be still, and the storm ceases, presenting rescue from the peril named in the preceding verse.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.14.30	Peter cries, \"save me\" as he sinks	The commentary describes a threatened person clinging for rescue; Peter begins to sink in the water and cries to Jesus to save him, making the appeal for refuge a physical scene.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Matt.14.31	Jesus catches Peter; faith and doubt	The commentary links iman with security; Jesus immediately catches Peter and names his little faith and doubt, showing rescue alongside a challenged trust.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.8.35	tribulation cannot separate believers from Christ's love	The commentary places humanity in loss; Paul asks whether distress, persecution, famine, nakedness, danger, or sword can separate those in Christ from his love, framing peril without surrender to loss.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.8.37	more than conquerors through the one who loves them	The commentary's exception describes people who escape loss; Paul says believers prevail amid these dangers through the one who loves them, specifying the source of security.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.8.38	death and life cannot separate	The commentary glosses khusr as perishing; Paul includes death and life among powers unable to separate believers from God's love, offering a concrete Christian claim against ultimate loss.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.8.39	nothing can separate from God's love	The commentary names iman as entry into safety; Paul's conclusion says no created thing can separate believers from God's love in Christ, making that safety comprehensive.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.5.7	cast anxieties on God	The commentary describes people in danger needing a refuge; Peter tells the community to cast all anxiety on God because he cares for them, making trust an act of placing burdens in protective hands.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.5.10	God restores after suffering	The commentary joins patience with calamity; Peter says that after brief suffering God will restore, strengthen, and establish the believers, giving endurance an outcome of stability.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Tim.3.15	God's household as pillar of truth	The commentary calls truth what must be protected; Paul describes the Church as God's household and the pillar and foundation of truth, combining community and safeguarding the truth.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Tim.1.14	guard the good deposit	The commentary says al-haqq is what a person is obliged to protect; Timothy is told to guard the entrusted good deposit through the Holy Spirit, making protection of teaching explicit.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jude.3	contend for the delivered faith	The commentary calls truth something to be guarded; Jude urges believers to contend for the faith once delivered to the saints, giving that protection a communal action.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Titus.1.9	hold fast the trustworthy word	The commentary links truth with what must be protected and shared; an overseer must hold fast the trustworthy word so he can exhort in sound teaching and refute contradiction.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.13.6	love rejoices with truth	The commentary says people mutually counsel one another in truth; Paul says love rejoices with the truth, placing truth inside the ethic governing a community.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.13.7	love endures all things	The commentary joins truth and patience as communal virtues; Paul describes love as bearing and enduring all things, giving patience a shared ethical setting.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.2	bear one another's burdens	The commentary calls the sabīr one who stands with the group in its affairs; Paul tells believers to carry one another's burdens, describing that solidarity as fulfilling Christ's law.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.12.26	one member's suffering is shared by all	The commentary describes a guarantor who stays with the community; Paul says when one member suffers, all suffer together, making communal presence concrete.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Jas.5.11	Job's endurance and the Lord's compassion	The commentary associates sabr with enduring calamity; James blesses those who endure and points to Job and the Lord's compassionate outcome, preserving both suffering and rescue.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.4.16	approach the throne for help in need	The commentary calls asr a refuge for a person in distress; Hebrews invites people to approach the throne of grace to receive mercy and timely help, presenting access to God as refuge.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1John.3.18	love in deed and truth	The commentary joins righteous action with truth; John says love must be shown in deed and truth rather than words alone, uniting the stanza's ethical features.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.15.58	labor in the Lord is not in vain	The commentary says humanity is in loss and names righteous deeds; Paul urges steadfastness and abundant work because labor in the Lord is not empty, directly countering the fear that good action is lost.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Pet.3.15	defense of hope with gentleness	The commentary says truth is what a person must protect; Peter tells believers to be ready to answer for their hope, with gentleness and respect, making public defense of faith a disciplined act.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.12.12	patient in tribulation; constant in prayer	The commentary links sabr with calamity and the believers' refuge with iman; Paul summarizes communal life as rejoicing in hope, being patient in tribulation, and persevering in prayer.
EOF"
